//: Incremental TypeScript adoption — a strangler, not a rewrite.
`allowJs` + `checkJs: false` means the 60-odd existing .jsx files are
compiled but NOT type-checked, so nothing that works today can start
failing. New and converted modules are .ts/.tsx and are checked fully.
The payoff lands at the API boundary: src/lib/api.d.ts declares every
export of lib/api.js, so importing a name that does not exist becomes a
compile error. That is exactly the class of bug that shipped as
`kbStatus` — DiscoveryV2 called a function it had never imported, the
call resolved to a useState variable, and an empty catch hid it.
Run `yarn typecheck` to check without building.
CRA rewrites a few of these fields on start; that is expected.
